text: Carpentry consists of a series of actions demanding precision and careful observation. Sanding occurs first to refine a board's surface until it reaches a manageable texture. Next, sawing takes place as a sharp blade slices through the timber. This cutting phase often requires several passes and exact measurements. Afterward, sanding resumes to clear away sawdust and debris for the intended finish. Such attention is vital because a board that has been cut and sanded properly will possess an excellent appearance and tactile quality once completed.
